prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by PROTACs, bifunctional molecules that bring a chosen protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase and cause its destruction

statement.case_for: After the full first round my preferred configuration is unchanged: B068 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, but with the citation now explicitly limited to PROTACs. The core claim is a measurable chemical one. A bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex, the target is ubiquitinated and degraded, and the molecule is recycled, so the effect is catalytic and event-driven. This has been reproduced independently across many targets and E3 ligases, and Ciulli's structural and biophysical work on VHL ligands and ternary-complex cooperativity supplies the quantitative chemistry that made the approach rational. It is also the only shortlisted achievement that seven of eight members place in their first choice or alternatives, and I weigh that as a signal of breadth only, not as scientific evidence. For my own field, degraders are already a routine tool for acutely removing replication and nucleotide-metabolism enzymes.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC has been approved, so the clinical validation that would settle maturity is missing, and a disappointing late-stage readout could make a 2026 prize look early. A PROTAC-only citation also leaves out the cereblon and thalidomide molecular-glue lineage (Handa, Ito, Kim, Sakamoto, Gray), which has the strongest link to approved drugs, and the three-name cap forces uncomfortable exclusions even within the PROTAC lineage, notably Sakamoto as author of the first small-molecule PROTAC. If a majority wants one citation that covers both degrader classes, my trio is the wrong one.

responses.point: Linke, as chair and first-choice supporter of B003, asks whether the demixing and multivalency principle can be cited without asserting that particular condensates are phase-separated in vivo, and names B068 as his first alternative.
responses.response: I accept that a principle-only citation is possible and that the 2009 P-granule work and Rosen's multivalent reconstitution give a dated origin. My difficulty is the standard I apply as an experimentalist: the physical chemistry is shown in vitro, while the biological claim, that cells use it, still depends on case-by-case evidence with overexpression artefacts. A citation that avoids the in vivo claim is honest, but it then rewards a principle whose consequences for cells are not settled. For degraders the cellular consequence has been measured directly, as target loss, in many systems. I therefore keep B003 as my first alternative and I would not block it if the committee words it as Linke proposes.

responses.point: Zou, supporting B009 with Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt, argues that nitrogenase rests on structures reproduced by several independent groups over three decades, and that B068 has broader opening support but a less settled attribution.
responses.response: Zou's point about independent reproduction is the criterion I care about most, and it is why I have moved B009 into my alternatives in place of base editing. The structure and cofactor claims are as firmly established as anything on the list. What keeps me from ranking it first is that the N2 reduction mechanism is unresolved, as he concedes, so the citation would stay at structure, and the five-name credit among Rees, Dean, Einsle, Seefeldt and Ribbe cannot be compressed cleanly into three. I do agree with him that the attribution problem for B068 is real, but I think it is a smaller one: Crews and Deshaies have a dated 2001 proof of concept, and the open question is only the third name.

responses.point: Aili, who shares my B068 trio, offers narrowing the citation to the PROTAC concept if the glue lineage cannot be resolved within three names, and notes that B003 or B060 might be safer on maturity.
responses.response: I agree with narrowing, and I have done it in my citation. I would not accept a version that implies the prize covers molecular glues, because that would credit Ciulli, Crews and Deshaies for the cereblon biology, which they did not do. On his maturity worry, I weigh B060 below B003 for the reason I gave in round 1, namely that credit among sequencing platforms is harder to settle than the degrader split, and I do not think B003 is safer on timing given the physiological-relevance dispute that Linke and Sparr themselves state.

responses.point: Aqvist backs base editing (B024) with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, but lists the 2020 CRISPR overlap, the Target-AID priority question with Kondo and Nishida, and the possible later case for prime editing as reservations.
responses.response: His own reservations have weakened B024 for me. A second genome-editing prize so soon after 2020, together with an unresolved priority question over Target-AID and the chance that prime editing is judged the more general advance, makes the base-editing configuration less stable than I treated it in round 1, so I have dropped it from my alternatives. I still regard a Liu-centred prize as a legitimate future option.

responses.point: Brzezinski, with Zou, supports nitrogenase and discloses that his preference partly reflects an interest in biological energy conversion.
responses.response: I appreciate the disclosure and do not see it as a conflict. It does not change my reading that the unresolved catalytic mechanism and the Dean and Einsle question for the third name are the real obstacles for B009. If the committee settles the third name and accepts a structure-and-cofactor citation, I would vote for it over B003.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a PROTAC-only citation, or require a combined degrader prize that adds Handa or Sakamoto.
Whether the missing PROTAC approval makes 2026 too early, and I have no evidence that settles this beyond the clinical pipeline described in the supplied material.
Whether Ciulli, Sakamoto or Handa is the best third name beside Crews and Deshaies.
My account of credit priority comes from memory of the literature and the supplied credit list, not independent verification.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no personal or institutional tie to the B068 candidates, or to the candidates on my alternative ballots. I know the replication and dNTP-metabolism communities that use degraders as tools, but that is not a collaboration with any candidate.
